_readme: The document control plane for retrieval. Every row names a real file in this directory and carries the access policy for it; the files themselves carry only content, with no marker of who may read them. That split is deliberate: policy lives in exactly one place a reviewer can audit, and adding a document is one file plus one row here, with no code change. Synthetic data about one fictional programme -- no real customer content belongs here.

_fields.document_id: Stable identifier, and the source_id every citation carries. Where a document backs a field the mock ERP also serves, this reuses that record's source_id from data/erp/project.json, so a tool answer and a retrieved passage name the same artifact.
_fields.path: Relative to this manifest. A row whose file is missing raises ManifestEntryError; documents are never silently skipped.
_fields.document_type: What class of document this is. Used for reporting and by any future index routing; never used to decide access.
_fields.project_code: Which project the content belongs to. Half of the authorization check.
_fields.required_scope: The one entitlement an actor must hold to read this document. Exactly one, so the rule is expressible as a vector-store filter and auditable as a single comparison. Namespaced by what it grants, matching the tool scopes in tools/registry.py.
_fields.classification: The human-facing sensitivity label. Recorded and shown, never the thing that grants or denies access -- required_scope is.
